intended_object: The determinant homomorphism det : K₁(R) = GL(R)^{ab} → Rˣ, for R a commutative ring. It is the stable determinant on GL(R) = colim GLₙ(R), factored through the abelianization. This reading comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
`det R` is the stable determinant on `StableGL R`. The file builds it with `lift` from the determinants of the finite-rank groups GLₙ(R), using `det_finStabilize`: stabilizing a matrix with an identity block does not change its determinant. `Abelianization.lift` turns any homomorphism into an abelian group into a homomorphism out of the abelianization, so applying it to `det R` gives the map K₁(R) → Rˣ with [g] ↦ det g. This is the standard construction.

The commutative ring hypothesis is the natural setting, because the determinant is only defined over commutative rings. The library's simp lemma `abelianizationDet_of` confirms that the map sends the class of g to det g. Mathlib has no stable general linear group and no K₁ determinant, so there is no more general counterpart.
